title: Streamline encoder+reranker registration and profile deployment for embeddings
creator: Priya Nair
description: Goal: Provide a single, auditable flow to register embedding encoders and pairwise rerankers into the model catalog, pin a production version, and publish performance profiles used by the Console and Optimize. Deliverables: (1) an onboarding CLI and API endpoint that accepts model metadata (architecture, quantization variants, tokenizer id), validation artifacts, and a canonical perf profile JSON; (2) a pinning API and UI surface to lock a model to a specific semantic version for serving; (3) a profile publisher service to atomically publish profiles for latency, throughput, and embed/rerank quality metrics; (4) a canary rollout path so we can route X% traffic to a new variant and automatically roll back on regressions. Out of scope for this ticket: end-to-end billing integration and SDK language bindings. Acceptance criteria: successful onboarding of new encoder+reranker pair (end-to-end) in staging, pinned version surfaced in Console, perf profile used by scheduler for kernel selection, canary rollout exercise documented and executed with rollback test.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Kickoff: aligned with Product and Design. Decided to use existing registry schema for base fields but extend with 'pairing' metadata for encoder->reranker links. Action: Priya to draft schema changes.

2026-02-24 - Schema proposal v0.1 posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Encoder-Reranker+Registry+Schema. Feedback from runtime team: prefer explicit 'kv_cache_compat' and 'max_seq_len' fields to drive kernel selection.

2026-03-01 - Design review: Design (Evelyn Chen) requested a clear UI element for 'pinned version' and 'canary %'. PM (Liam O'Connor) asked for audit log entries for pin/unpin actions. Action: Diego to prototype API surfaces and update PRD.

2026-03-05 - Engineering notes: Implemented onboarding API endpoint + validation harness. Initial failure modes: tokenizer mismatch detection surfaced late; added extra validation step to reject models without tokenizer mapping.
2026-03-08 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8341 - onboarding endpoint + registry migration. Requesting review from @asha and @marina.

2026-03-10 - CI: integration tests added for profile publish and pin flow. Discovered race when publishing profile while a canary rollout is in-flight. Decided to serialize profile publish operations per model key. Diego filed follow-up: ENG-16921.

2026-03-12 - Canary plan agreed: initial rollout 5% for 2 hours with automated latency/quality checks (benchmarks in Optimize). If regression > 3% in rerank nDCG or 10% in p95 latency, auto rollback. Related doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/Onboarding-Canary-Runbook
notes: Trade-offs: we chose to reuse the existing catalog to accelerate rollout; downside is added schema complexity for pairing and quantization variants. Long-term plan is a lightweight model manifest that can be stored with model artifacts (ENG-17050).
testing_plan: 1) Unit test schema validation and tokenizer mapping 2) Integration test that exercises registry -> scheduler mapping for kernel selection 3) End-to-end staging run: upload model pair, publish profile, pin version, execute canary and trigger rollback criteria 4) Postmortem checklist and SLO alert tuning
engineering_notes: Scheduler integration required adding a 'preferred_kernel' hint in profile JSON. Also added support for 'quantization_variants' so profile publisher can attach perf numbers per quantized artifact. Will add metric tags to make per-customer routing decisions easier.
rollout_strategy: staging -> internal canary (5%) -> gradual 25% over 48h -> full. Automated checks at each stage with manual approval gates after 25%.
acceptance_criteria: Model pair can be onboarded via CLI and API with validation artifacts
Pinned version is displayed in Console and prevents accidental rollout of non-pinned variants
Performance profile is published and consumed by the scheduler for kernel selection
Canary rollout exercises auto-rollback on defined quality/latency thresholds
